title: Madoka Magica’s Big Film Trilogy Is Going to Be Easier to Watch Than Ever
content:
After more than 12 years, the film trilogy of Puella Magi Madoka Magica will officially be streaming on Netflix. The films were originally released in 2012 and 2013, and now the official X handle of Netflix Anime has confirmed the platform will be adding these movies to its library next year. The post hasn’t shared an exact release date yet, but it will make its debut in January 2027 with all-new dubs in Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. While the streaming announcement is surely exciting, the new dubs are the most exciting part. Madoka Magica is a critically acclaimed fantasy classic on Crunchyroll with a surprise dark twist beneath its cheerful facade.

Crunchyroll has been the primary home of the anime for over a decade now, but Netflix has only made it easier to watch. The story centers around magical girls and remains one of the most shocking series of all time. The award-winning show released its anime debut in 2011 before returning with sequel movies in 2012 and 2013 . The franchise is getting a major revival this year, which is all the more reason why Netflix is all set to make this series more accessible to fans.

Puella Magi Madoka Magica ‘s Revival Movie Is Coming to U.S. Theatres

In 2021, the anime announced a revival film, Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie – Walpurgisnacht: Rising , to commemorate the 10th anniversary, but it was hit with several delays. The film was expected to be released in 2024, but after an unexpected delay, it finally hit Japanese theaters in August this year. The movie will be coming to theaters across North America for a limited time from January 16th to 19th, 2027. The latest movie serves as an official sequel to the 2013 film and confirms the return of the staff members and voice actors from the original story. Although there’s still a while before fans can watch the latest movie, fans can catch up with the trilogy in the meantime. Before Netflix debuts the trilogy, Crunchyroll will begin streaming the movies for the first time on November 8th, 2026.

What Is the Latest Madoka Magica Movie About?

The story is focused primarily on Homura as she aims to uncover the truth behind the mysterious circumstances. Homura senses something ominous beneath the peaceful atmosphere while others remain oblivious to the danger in front of them. As her suspicion grows, she notices that someone who shouldn’t even exist is living among them and joining in on their daily routine, while remaining inconspicuous. The latest film will pick up the story from where the previous film left off, bringing a new set of challenges for the girls. The latest movie is more exciting than ever, with new plot twists, more visually polished animation, and another exciting story. Since it’s based on an original story, the delay was initially disappointing, especially considering there’s no way to know what to expect from the movie. However, the movie was a massive success in Japanese theatres, and fans’ hopes are higher than ever right now.

title: The Remarried Empress to Make Anime Debut With Crunchyroll in 2027 – Watch First Look Trailer
content:
The Remarried Empress is finally getting an anime adaptation after its controversial light novel and manhwa. The webtoon industry is on the rise thanks to several anime adaptations. Crunchyroll has played a huge role in giving these anime a global platform, especially after the success of Solo Leveling and many such series. However, so far, a majority of the webtoon adaptations have been action fantasies, focusing on either an underdog or an overpowered protagonist. Things have slightly begun to change after the recent wave of announcements by Crunchyroll regarding the webtoon adaptations. One of the biggest new projects will be The Remarried Empress, a popular romance fantasy full of palace drama.

The series was first released as a manhwa and light novel around the same month. While the manhwa and light novel have already ended, fans have something new to look forward to next year with the anime debut. Not to mention that the series is also getting a live-action adaptation thanks to its massive popularity. The anime’s trailer has already been revealed, and it shares a brief glimpse at what to expect from the story and the visuals. Of course, since the announcement has only been made, it doesn’t reveal all the details regarding the series yet.

The Remarried Empress Anime Debut Drops First Trailer

The trailer introduces the main characters, Navier, Sovieshu, Henry, and Rashta. While the special promo trailer doesn’t give a broader look at the story, it confirms that Henry, a king from a neighboring country, will be the main lead. The story primarily focuses on Navier , an Empress, who couldn’t tolerate her husband welcoming a slave girl, Rashta, as his concubine and accepted a divorce. However, on the day of the divorce, she also announced her marriage to King Henry. The story features palace politics, schemes, and tragedy, along with supernatural elements. Considering that Crunchyroll has been pushing the anime adaptations of webtoons and the official YouTube channel shared the trailer, there’s no doubt what the streaming platform will be. The anime will premiere next year, although the exact release date hasn’t been revealed yet.

Why Is The Remarried Empress Controversial?

As popular as the anime is, it also gets its fair share of hate due to villainizing a young slave girl while an older, privileged Empress is the victim. The story glosses over the issues of slavery while treating them as inferior to ordinary citizens. While the story stays true to its themes, considering how the royalty will be blind to the suffering of the less privileged and even look down on them, many readers criticize the thoughtless portrayal of sensitive themes. The story is mainly about how Navier, who lived a picture-perfect life as she was born in a noble family with a long line of empresses. Since she was a child, she knew the path she would take, but her life came crashing down when the Emperor fell for his concubine. Instead of accepting her fate, she remarries Henry and moves to another kingdom.

title: 3 Anime of 2026 That Are the Perfect Replacements for Solo Leveling Fans
content:
Solo Leveling has emerged as one of the leading anime franchises in the industry since its debut in 2024. By adapting the famous webcomic, the anime introduced fans to what made the series so popular as a manhwa. Ultimately, the series revolves around a unique opportunity that transforms the protagonist’s life, allowing him to embark on a journey of self-growth. Other elements, such as its RPG-style video game mechanics, are also among its biggest highlights.

With Solo Leveling executing these elements so flawlessly, fans are left craving more. Following the anime’s debut and the conclusion of its second season, it is only natural for fans to seek out similar series. The anime industry seems to recognize this demand, as more adaptations of Korean webcomics have emerged. This year alone, one anime premiered in the Summer season, while two more are currently airing in Fall 2026, giving fans potential replacements for Solo Leveling .

3) The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life

One of the most intriguing elements of Solo Leveling is its power fantasy. After receiving an incredible gift following an intriguing encounter, the series focuses on how the protagonist uses his newfound power. Jinwoo embarks on a journey to seriously hone his abilities, with this seriousness becoming a defining element of the show. This is exactly what makes The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life a potential replacement for Solo Leveling , offering a hilarious twist on the same concept.

The anime features an enhancer named Rein, who is kicked out of his guild party because its members’ weapons have already reached their maximum potential. Rein takes the enhancement skills he used to upgrade others’ weapons and applies them to a copper sword, making it so powerful that nothing can stand in his way. However, instead of seeking revenge, Rein embarks on a carefree journey, embracing a laid-back and unserious approach rather than the seriousness of Solo Leveling . This makes the series a refreshing change for fans.

2) Overgeared

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life isn’t the only currently airing anime to take a fun approach to Solo Leveling ; Overgeared also stands out with its portrayal of a desperate yet hilariously unserious protagonist , which serves as the anime’s comedic element. The series embraces the leveling-up concept through a game system that, in this fantastical world, also affects the real world.

The protagonist, whose in-game name is Grid, hilariously portrays a man desperate for success, being a 25-year-old with nothing going on in his life. As Grid continues to lose even more money in the game, he gets an opportunity to change his class, becoming a Blacksmith and inheriting the abilities of a legendary blacksmith. Yet, even after acquiring an overpowered class, Grid never loses his desperation, making the anime hilarious and setting it apart from Solo Leveling .

1) Tomb Raider King

The anime most notably compared to Solo Leveling this year is Tomb Raider King , thanks to its many similar elements right from the start, particularly its character designs, which make several characters look strikingly similar across the two series. However, Tomb Raider King also has its own unique elements. One of the best is its protagonist, Seo Jooheon, who is much older and has already experienced betrayal in the future.

As a result, the second chance he receives feels more personal, and Jooheon makes no effort to hide that he is on a journey of revenge and intends to conquer everything in his path. Another standout element is the series’ use of relics inspired by historical artifacts, which also adds an educational aspect to the story. With 12 episodes in its first season, Tomb Raider King is undoubtedly one of the most similar anime to Solo Leveling that fans can watch in 2026.

title: One Piece Just Set Up Another Dive Into the Most Tragic Straw Hat’s Painful Past For a Good Reason
content:
One Piece is currently depicting the Elbaph arc, which has reached a crucial stage in its climax, positioning the Straw Hats to evolve and gain new power upgrades to confront the new villains. In the latest chapter, after confirming Zoro’s power upgrade, the series is now beginning to set up the next prominent crew member to receive an upgrade. As most shonen series do, it is revisiting the character’s past to set up a significant power boost. The Straw Hat in question is none other than Sanji, the third-strongest member of the crew, who also has one of the most tragic pasts.

Initially, the series revealed that Sanji was an orphan and that Captain Zeff sacrificed his leg to ensure Sanji’s survival. While this established Sanji’s traumatic past, nothing could have prepared fans for the revelations in One Piece ‘s Whole Cake Island arc , which revealed that he was part of the Vinsmoke family and had been tortured and experimented on for years simply because he was kind and loving toward his sick mother. This trauma ultimately led him to learn how to cook. Now, it seems the series is revisiting his past and another significant event to help Sanji gain the power needed to fight the God’s Knights, who can only be defeated by Conqueror’s Haki.

One Piece Has Confirmed the Next Straw Hat to Get a Power Upgrade by Revisiting a Specific Past

While the One Piece series has always hinted that Zoro possesses Conqueror’s Haki , Sanji has been positioned away from this power. However, now that it has become significant for defeating the final villains, and Sanji is nowhere near demonstrating that he can wield Conqueror’s Haki, it was intriguing to see how he would manage to do so. Now, in the latest chapter, One Piece Chapter 1195, the series has confirmed that the answer may lie in Sanji’s past, which has yet to be fully depicted. Sanji has constantly harbored a personality that leads him to underestimate himself, and he recalls this in the latest chapter as well, with several panels depicting his past trauma and how he was ready to sacrifice himself.

However, in the final moments of the latest chapter, Sanji is reminded of his time on Momoiro Island, where he trained for two years during the timeskip and developed all sorts of techniques. But the memory Sanji is recalling is something he had deliberately suppressed for some reason, and the latest chapter hilariously hints that his entire training session on Momoiro Island was hell for him. The Queen of the Kamabakka Kingdom, Emporio Ivankov, appears in this flashback, telling Sanji that he has a serious weakness . Considering that Sanji had deliberately suppressed his memories of the island, it still hints that he had the worst time there.

Sanji’s training on this island has never been depicted in detail before, as it was hilariously established that he developed all these techniques to keep the island’s drag queens away from him. However, his two years of growth are important, and the weakness Ivankov calls out, which Sanji has likely since overcome, could be the key to defeating the God’s Knights. Sanji’s upgrade has been due in One Piece for a long time, and it seems the creator may have been planning his comeback in a unique way. It looks like Sanji’s next power-up could revisit a traumatic event from his past that readers might find amusing, giving the Straw Hats’ cook his own unique upgrade separate from Zoro and Luffy.

title: Killing Bites Manga Publishes 1st Part of Final Chapter
content:
Sentai Filmworks licensed the television anime adaptation of the manga, and it describes the story:

By the time Yuya Nomoto discovers his so-called friends have duped him into a clandestine plot to kidnap a high school girl, they're already dead. Things go from bad to worse as Yuya is dragged into a cutthroat world of underground bloodsport known as Killing Bites, where Therianthropes — brutal gene-edited killing machines — fight to the death for rival, power-hungry forces who manipulate society from the shadows.

Murata and Sumita launched the manga in Monthly Hero's in March 2017, although it now runs on the Comiplex website. Hero's Inc. published the manga's 27th compiled book volume on June 29. Mangamo acquired the manga.

The television anime adaptation premiered on the Animeism programming block on MBS and TBS in January 2018. The anime's unaired "director's cut" streamed worldwide on Amazon Prime Video . The anime had 12 episodes.

title: Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Won’t Be as “New” as Fans Might Want
content:
Dragon Ball Super has returned after eight years with a new remake anime series , but one star revealed that this new anime unfortunately won’t be as “new” as fans are hoping for. Dragon Ball Super ‘s original TV anime made its debut over a decade ago, and it’s been eight years since the Tournament of Power. Though Dragon Ball has continued with new movies and TV projects in that time since, there’s something special about Dragon Ball Super returning for new episodes that have been retooled for the modern era.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is an “enhanced” version of the original TV series touting new visuals, re-cut sequences, sound effects and more . But in an official interview for the new series’ premiere (as shared via press release), Beerus voice actor Koichi Yamadera revealed that he has not done any new voice work for the remake series. So while it’s set to feature some new animated sequences and more (which have already been seen in the premiere episode), it’s at least confirmed that one member of the original voice cast hasn’t recorded for any new material.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Will Be Reusing Original TV Anime Voice Lines

When Yamadera was asked about the new Dragon Ball Super: Beerus series , the Beerus voice star was delighted to find out that the anime would be continuing and even feature his character in the title. But the more surprising development was that Yamadera revealed that the team didn’t record any new dialogue, “And then I heard we wouldn’t be recording new dialogue, which surprised me even more.” As the way the star broke it down, it’s going to be a re-edit of that original TV series audio to make something new, “They’re taking what we recorded back then and building something new out of it — it felt like a stroke of luck.”

Yamadera detailing the process here could just be a confirmation that he was the only one to not record any new audio, but it’s likely that the production on a whole has been treated in this matter. It seems like Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be using the voice lines from the original Dragon Ball Super TV anime, and any brand new scenes will not require any additional voice work . This can be heard with the return of late voice actors Unsho Ishizuka (Mr. Satan) and Joji Yanami (King Kai) in the premiere, who have tragically passed since the end of the original series.

What Does This Mean for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ‘ Future?

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has raised a few questions about its future Yamadera revealing that there won’t be any new voice lines, and that likely means that these enhancements to the original series won’t be as expansive as fans might have hoped to see from the franchise’s big return. There had been lofty dreams about the kinds of new additions that could have been added such as fans wanting more of the manga material included before the debut of Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol in the future .

But this also raises questions about the scope of this new remake. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has yet to confirm how many episodes it’s going to be running for , but it will be showcasing new takes on the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs. Even if it uses the same voice lines from the original series, there’s a hope that enough has changed about its reorganization and visual upgrades that it still feels new either way.

How does this make you feel about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ? How are you liking the premiere of the remake anime series so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has raised a few questions about its future Yamadera revealing that there won’t be any new voice lines, and that likely means that these enhancements to the original series won’t be as expansive as fans might have hoped to see from the franchise’s big return. There had been lofty dreams about the kinds of new additions that could have been added such as fans wanting more of the manga material included before the debut of Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol in the future .

But this also raises questions about the scope of this new remake. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has yet to confirm how many episodes it’s going to be running for , but it will be showcasing new takes on the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs. Even if it uses the same voice lines from the original series, there’s a hope that enough has changed about its reorganization and visual upgrades that it still feels new either way.
How does this make you feel about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ? How are you liking the premiere of the remake anime series so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Osamu Tezuka's Phoenix Manga's Future Arc Gets Stage Play in February
content:
Osamu Tezuka 's Phoenix ( Hi no Tori ) manga is inspiring another stage play that will run at Sakura Hall in Shibuya Cultural Centre Owada in Tokyo from February 6-8. The play Hi no Tori Mirai-hen ZEROMDISTANCE ( Phoenix Future Arc ZEROMDISTANCE) adapts the manga's "Future" arc.

The play stars Jutta Yuki as Masato, Narumi Yasuda as the voice of the Phoenix , Moro Morooka as Dr. Saruta, Adone Kudō and Shiina Yuzuki as Tamami, and Kaiki Ohara as Rock.

Ryusei Kudoh is directing and writing the play. He is also serving as executive producer. Ryo Oguri is producing. Nao'ymt is handling the music.

Tezuka wrote Phoenix 's "Future" arc between December 1967 and September 1968. The official Osamu Tezuka website describes the second part:

Set in A.D. 3404, the earth is dying, and human beings inhabit a city-state built deep under the ground. The authorities search for Yamanobe Masato, Class 2 space warrior of Megalopolis Yamato. They suspect him of hiding Tamami, a girl transformed into a human from her original form as the outer space creature Moopie. Masato and Tamami escape over deserted land to flee from their country. Guided by the Phoenix , they arrive at Dr. Saruta's dome. Here, Dr. Saruta conducts research on artificial life with the aim of bringing extinct creatures back. Meanwhile, the final war of the human race begins in the underground city, and humans become extinct.

The manga recently inspired a stage play that ran at Theatre West at the Tokyo Metropolitan Theater in July 2024. The play was based on the manga's "Karma" arc ("Hō-ō-hen," or literally "Firebird Arc")

Phoenix inspired a live manga performance Mangalogue: Hi no Tori that ran from April 22-May 16 at MoN Takanawa: The Museum of Narratives' Box1000 theaters.

Tezuka continued to serialize new arcs for the manga until the 12th part, "Sun," which ended in 1988, the year before his death. The stories presented in the Phoenix manga span multiple eras, past and future.

Kodansha USA Publishing licensed the manga. The first Deluxe Edition print volume includes the "Dawn" and "Future" arcs.

Viz Media previously published the manga in North America.

The four-episode Phoenix: Eden17 anime based on the manga debuted worldwide on Disney+ in September 2023. The anime's Japanese title is Hi no Tori: Eden no Sora (literally, Phoenix : Eden's Space). The anime also got a film version in November 2023 titled Phoenix: Reminiscence of Flower ( Hi no Tori: Eden no Hana , literally "Eden's Flower"). The film features a different ending from the Phoenix: Eden17 anime. The anime is based on the "Nostalgia" arc of the original manga.

The manga also inspired a series of anime film and OVA adaptations from 1978 to 1987, each adapting a different story in the manga. The manga inspired a 2004 television anime.

title: Kagurabachi Confirms End Date for Anime World Tour With Final Stops Revealed
content:
Kagurabachi has been in the midst of a world tour where the anime has been sharing the first episode before anywhere else, and now a date has been set for its grand finale with the final stops on the tour revealed. Takeru Hokazono’s Kagurabachi manga is now celebrating its 3rd anniversary of its original debut with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, and it’s going to go all out with the highly anticipated release of its upcoming anime adaptation next year.

Kagurabachi has been on a world tour for the past few months across major events and countries where lucky fans in attendance had been treated to the early premiere of the anime’s very first episode. But as one of the major updates shared during Shueisha’s latest Jump Press livestream this week , Kagurabachi has now confirmed that it’s going to round out the World Tour with a few more stops before it ends in Japan next March.

Kagurabachi World Tour to End in Japan March 2027

As detailed via press release, the Kagurabachi World Tour is expanding with a Part 3 that will take it to some big new locations over the rest of the year with planned stops at AFA Singapore on November 29th, a stop over in Seoul planned for December 6th, and a stop at CCXP Brazil with no date or time confirmed for it thus far. The tour has been going across multiple countries and events since it kicked off earlier this July, and will be wrapping up with some huge plans for its own world premiere screening when it finally comes back to Japan.

The finale for the Kagurabachi World Tour Event will be taking place on Thursday, March 25 in Japan, and will not only feature the world premiere of the first full episode (instead of just 20 minutes as seen with the other stops) but the second episode as well. It’s also teased that members of the production staff and voice cast will also be in attendance for this grand finale, and that makes a ton of sense considering the actual premiere of the anime series will be coming soon after some time in April as part of the Spring 2027 anime schedule.

When Does Kagurabachi’ s Anime Come Out?

Kagurabachi is now scheduled for a release sometime in April as part of the Spring 2027 anime schedule. While no concrete release date has been announced for the series as of this time, it has been confirmed to be streaming with Crunchyroll outside of Japan when it hits. The anime will be directed by Tetsuya Takeuchi for Cypic (who provided a special illustration for the manga’s third anniversary you can check out above) with Keigo Sasaki providing the character designs, but there are still many secrets being kept about how the new series has been coming along thus far.

Kagurabachi will be revealing even more soon enough as not only can fans look forward to more of this world tour, but the franchise has been confirmed to be one of the many titles with something to showcase as part of Jump Festa 2027 later this December . This would likely be the best time for a major update for the anime outside of the coming world tour stops, so hopefully we’ll get something big then. Are you going to try and make it to one of these final Kagurabachi world tour stops? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Texas' Kawacon Anime, Gaming Convention Ends After 5 Years
content:
The staff of the convention did not announce a reason but did make a statement:

To our Kawacon family, After much consideration and with heavy hearts, we have made the difficult decision to cease Kawacon operations for the foreseeable future. Over the past five years, Kawacon has grown into something far beyond what we originally imagined. What started as a vision became a thriving community that brought thousands of people together through their shared love of fandom, creativity, and connection. From our very first event to Kawacon 5, every year brought unforgettable memories, lasting friendships, and experiences we will always cherish. We are incredibly proud of everything we accomplished together. To our attendees, artists, exhibitors, guests, volunteers, staff, sponsors, and everyone who supported us along the way: Thank you. Your passion and dedication made Kawacon what it became, and we couldn't have done it without you. From the bottom of our hearts, thank you for believing in our vision, growing alongside us, and making these past five years so special. Until we meet again. - The Kawacon Team

The first Kawacon event took place in February 2026.
